title: Ruth Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ruth chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ruth Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ruth Chapter 4.

questions.question: Where did Boaz go and sit before speaking to the kinsman?
questions.correctAnswer: At the gate
questions.explanation: Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there before the kinsman came by, as stated in Ruth 4:1.

questions.question: How many elders of the city did Boaz take to sit with them?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten
questions.explanation: Boaz took ten men of the elders of the city and told them to sit down, as mentioned in Ruth 4:2.

questions.question: What was Naomi selling when Boaz spoke to the kinsman?
questions.correctAnswer: A parcel of land
questions.explanation: Naomi was selling a parcel of land that belonged to their brother Elimelech, as explained in Ruth 4:3.

questions.question: What did Boaz tell the kinsman to do regarding the land?
options: Buy it before the inhabitants and elders
questions.correctAnswer: Buy it before the inhabitants and elders
questions.explanation: Boaz told the kinsman to buy the land before the inhabitants and elders, as stated in Ruth 4:4.

questions.question: Who did Boaz say the kinsman must also buy the land from when buying Naomi’s land?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth the Moabitess
questions.explanation: Boaz said the kinsman must buy the land also from Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the dead man's name, as mentioned in Ruth 4:5.

questions.question: Why did the kinsman refuse to redeem the land for himself?
options: He would mar his own inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: He would mar his own inheritance
questions.explanation: The kinsman refused because he said he could not redeem it for himself lest he mar his own inheritance, as stated in Ruth 4:6.

questions.question: What action was used in Israel to confirm redeeming and changing things?
options: Plucking off a shoe and giving it to a neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: Plucking off a shoe and giving it to a neighbor
questions.explanation: The manner to confirm redeeming was to pluck off a shoe and give it to the neighbor as testimony, as explained in Ruth 4:7.

questions.question: What did the kinsman do to Boaz to show he relinquished his right to redeem?
questions.correctAnswer: Drew off his shoe
questions.explanation: The kinsman drew off his shoe and gave it to Boaz to confirm the transaction, as stated in Ruth 4:8.

questions.question: True or False: Boaz sat down first and then called the kinsman to sit by him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Boaz went up to the gate, sat down, and then called the kinsman to come and sit, as described in Ruth 4:1.

questions.question: True or False: The kinsman immediately refused to redeem Naomi’s land.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The kinsman initially said he would redeem it, but later refused because it would mar his own inheritance, as shown in Ruth 4:4 and 4:6.

questions.question: True or False: The elders of the city were called to witness the transaction.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Boaz took ten elders of the city to sit and witness the transaction, as stated in Ruth 4:2.

questions.question: True or False: The kinsman gave Boaz his ring as a testimony of redeeming the land.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The testimony was given by plucking off a shoe, not a ring, as described in Ruth 4:7-8.

questions.question: Who did Boaz say he was after in right to redeem the land?
questions.correctAnswer: The kinsman
questions.explanation: Boaz said he was after the kinsman in right to redeem the land, as stated in Ruth 4:4.

questions.question: Which of these events happened first in Ruth 4?
options: Boaz told the kinsman to buy the land
Boaz called ten elders to sit
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz sat at the gate
questions.explanation: First, Boaz went up to the gate and sat down (Ruth 4:1), before calling the kinsman, telling him to buy the land, or calling the elders.

questions.question: What relationship did Boaz identify the land as belonging to?
questions.correctAnswer: Elimelech, their brother
questions.explanation: Boaz identified the land as that of their brother Elimelech, as mentioned in Ruth 4:3.

medium.title: Ruth Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ruth Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Boaz declare to the elders and all the people at the gate?
options: He had bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's, and Mahlon's from Naomi
He was going to sell a parcel of land in Moab
He refused to marry Ruth the Moabitess
He was moving to Bethlehem alone
questions.correctAnswer: He had bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's, and Mahlon's from Naomi
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:9 states that Boaz told the elders and all the people that he had bought all that belonged to Elimelech and his sons from Naomi, showing his legal claim and responsibility.

questions.question: According to Ruth 4:10, why did Boaz purchase Ruth the Moabitess as his wife?
options: To raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
To make her queen of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: To raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:10 explains Boaz's purpose for marrying Ruth was to preserve the name and inheritance of Mahlon, her deceased husband, preventing it from being cut off among his brethren.

questions.question: How did the people and elders respond to Boaz's declaration about Ruth and the land?
options: They said, 'We are witnesses' and blessed Boaz
They refused to witness the transaction
They asked Boaz to leave the city
They requested a higher price for the land
questions.correctAnswer: They said, 'We are witnesses' and blessed Boaz
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:11 records the people's response as affirming they were witnesses and blessing Boaz, likening the woman to Rachel and Leah who built Israel's house, emphasizing community support and blessing.

questions.question: What blessing did the elders and people invoke upon Boaz's house in Ruth 4:12?
options: That his house be like the house of Pharez, born to Judah by Tamar
questions.correctAnswer: That his house be like the house of Pharez, born to Judah by Tamar
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:12 contains the blessing that Boaz's house be like Pharez's, a significant ancestor of Judah, symbolizing continued blessing and legacy from God's providence.

questions.question: What was the outcome after Boaz took Ruth as his wife according to Ruth 4:13?
options: The LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son
Ruth returned to Naomi's house alone
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:13 describes how Boaz married Ruth and God blessed their union with a son, demonstrating God's providential care and faithfulness in their lineage.

questions.question: Based on Ruth 4:14, what did the women say to Naomi about the LORD's provision?
options: The LORD has not left Naomi without a kinsman
The LORD will destroy Naomi's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has not left Naomi without a kinsman
questions.explanation: In Ruth 4:14, the women bless the LORD for providing Naomi a kinsman-redeemer, ensuring her family line and name would continue and be honored in Israel.

questions.question: What role does the son born to Ruth and Boaz play in Naomi's life according to Ruth 4:15?
options: He shall be a restorer and nourisher of Naomi's life and old age
He will become a king of Israel
He will leave Naomi to live elsewhere
He is a stranger to Naomi
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be a restorer and nourisher of Naomi's life and old age
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:15 emphasizes the son's role in restoring Naomi's life and providing comfort in her old age, showing the importance of family and loyalty.

questions.question: How did Naomi respond to the birth of the child, as described in Ruth 4:16?
options: She took the child into her bosom and became its nurse
She gave the child to Boaz to raise
questions.correctAnswer: She took the child into her bosom and became its nurse
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:16 shows Naomi's tender care as she embraces the child and nurtures him, reflecting her restored joy and the community's blessing upon her.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name given to the child in Ruth 4:17?
options: The child was named Obed, father of Jesse, father of David
The child was named Mahlon after his grandfather
The child was named Boaz after his father
The child was named Elimelech after Naomi's husband
questions.correctAnswer: The child was named Obed, father of Jesse, father of David
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:17 identifies the child as Obed, linking him directly to the lineage of David, underscoring God's providence in the messianic line.

questions.question: What does the lineage recorded from Pharez to David in Ruth 4:18-22 teach us about God's plan?
options: God's plan is fulfilled through human generations with faithfulness
Pharez was the last ancestor of David
questions.correctAnswer: God's plan is fulfilled through human generations with faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:18-22 traces the genealogy from Pharez to David, highlighting God's sovereign plan unfolding through faithful human generations culminating in King David.

questions.question: True or False: The kinsman who first had the right to redeem the land chose to redeem it himself.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:6 explains the kinsman declined to redeem the land because it might harm his own inheritance, thus allowing Boaz to redeem it instead.

questions.question: True or False: The removal of the shoe was a legal testimony in Israel to confirm the redemption of property.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:7 states that removing and giving the shoe to a neighbor was a customary testimony confirming redemption or transfer of property rights in Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Ruth 4:11 shows the people prayed for Boaz to be famous in Bethlehem and compared Ruth to Rachel and Leah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:11 includes the people's blessing that the LORD make Ruth like Rachel and Leah, who built the house of Israel, and that Boaz be famous in Bethlehem, expressing hope for fruitfulness and honor.

questions.question: What does Ruth 4:10 promise will happen if Boaz buys the field from Naomi?
options: He must also take Ruth, the widow of Mahlon, to raise up her husband's name
He will become the richest man in Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: He must also take Ruth, the widow of Mahlon, to raise up her husband's name
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:10 teaches that redeeming the land includes marrying Ruth to preserve the deceased's name and inheritance, emphasizing responsibility and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Ruth 4:14-15 illustrate the virtue of loyalty within family relationships?
options: Naomi's daughter-in-law's love surpasses that of seven sons, bringing restoration and nourishment
Naomi is abandoned by all her family
Naomi curses Ruth for her actions
questions.correctAnswer: Naomi's daughter-in-law's love surpasses that of seven sons, bringing restoration and nourishment
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:14-15 praises Ruth's loyal love to Naomi as better than seven sons, showing how steadfast commitment restores and nourishes life, highlighting faithfulness and care.

hard.title: Ruth Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ruth Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who is named as the father of David in Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesse
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:17 states that Obed is the father of Jesse, and Jesse is the father of David.

questions.question: Which ancestor in Ruth 4 is directly linked to Tamar's lineage?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharez
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:12 references Pharez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, linking the genealogy back to Tamar.

questions.question: What is the significance of Boaz redeeming the land and marrying Ruth according to Ruth 4?
options: To raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
To please the elders of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: To raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:5 and 4:10 explain that Boaz redeems the land and marries Ruth to preserve the name of Mahlon, the dead relative, ensuring his inheritance continues.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently displayed in the genealogy from Pharez to David in Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The genealogy in Ruth 4:18-22 shows a chiastic structure linking key figures in a mirrored arrangement to emphasize David’s lineage.

questions.question: What does the act of plucking off the shoe symbolize in Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Transfer of redemption rights
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:7-8 explains that removing the shoe was a customary testimony in Israel to confirm the transfer of redemption rights.

questions.question: Which of these biblical books also emphasizes the theme of kinsman redeemer similar to Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus
questions.explanation: Leviticus 25 discusses the laws of redemption and the kinsman redeemer, which is a central theme in Ruth 4:3-6.

questions.question: Who did the elders and all the people in the gate bless in Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz and Ruth
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:11 records the blessing by the elders and people upon Boaz and Ruth, wishing them to be like Rachel and Leah who built Israel.

questions.question: What role does Naomi play after the birth of Obed in Ruth 4?
options: She became the nurse of the child
questions.correctAnswer: She became the nurse of the child
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:16 clearly states that Naomi took Obed into her bosom and became his nurse.

questions.question: Which phrase best describes the meaning of the Hebrew word 'Goel' that relates to Boaz in Ruth 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Kinsman redeemer
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Goel' means kinsman redeemer, describing Boaz’s role in redeeming Naomi's family (Ruth 4:1-6).

questions.question: Which New Testament figure is genealogically linked to Ruth 4's final verse?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:22 ends the genealogy with David, from whose line Jesus Christ is descended (Matthew 1:1-16).

questions.question: True or False: According to Ruth 4, Boaz redeemed the land but did not marry Ruth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:13 states that Boaz took Ruth as his wife after redeeming the land.

questions.question: True or False: The women in the gate named the son born to Naomi 'Obed' as recorded in Ruth 4.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:17 confirms that the women neighbors named the son Obed, recognizing him as born to Naomi.

questions.question: What is the cultural significance of redeeming a relative’s land in the context of Ruth 4?
options: To acquire new land for oneself
To transfer ownership to the king
questions.correctAnswer: To keep family inheritance intact
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:3-6 shows that the kinsman redeemer’s role was to preserve the family’s inheritance and name by redeeming land and marrying the widow.

questions.question: Which Old Testament story does the blessing in Ruth 4:11 allude to by mentioning Rachel and Leah?
options: The founding of Israel's twelve tribes
questions.correctAnswer: The founding of Israel's twelve tribes
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:11 refers to Rachel and Leah, the matriarchs who bore the twelve tribes of Israel, emphasizing the importance of lineage and legacy.

questions.question: How does the genealogy in Ruth 4 contribute to the author's purpose for the original audience?
options: To demonstrate God’s providence in preserving the Messianic line
To show the political power of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate God’s providence in preserving the Messianic line
questions.explanation: The genealogy in Ruth 4:18-22 highlights God’s providential care in preserving David’s royal line through Ruth, a Moabitess, providing hope and legitimacy to the original audience.

theological.title: Ruth Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ruth Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What legal act symbolized the transfer of redemption rights in ancient Israel as described in Ruth 4?
options: Plucking off and giving a shoe
Offering a lamb as a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Plucking off and giving a shoe
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:7 clearly states that the custom to confirm redemption involved a man plucking off his shoe and giving it to his neighbor as a testimony.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Boaz's willingness to redeem Naomi's land and marry Ruth to raise up the name of the dead?
options: Doctrine of redemption and covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of redemption and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:4-5 shows Boaz acting as a kinsman-redeemer, a picture of God's covenant faithfulness to redeem and preserve His people, reflecting the doctrine of redemption.

questions.question: How does Ruth 4:13 demonstrate God's providential blessing in the narrative?
options: God gave Ruth conception and she bore a son
God sent a prophet to Boaz
God destroyed the land of Moab
God made Boaz king of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: God gave Ruth conception and she bore a son
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:13 explicitly notes that the LORD gave Ruth conception and she bore a son, showing God's providential hand in blessing their union and continuing the lineage.

questions.question: According to Ruth 4:14-15, what role does the birth of Obed serve in Naomi's life?
options: Restorer of her life and a nourisher of her old age
questions.correctAnswer: Restorer of her life and a nourisher of her old age
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:14-15 describes Obed as the restorer and nourisher of Naomi's life and old age, indicating God's restorative grace in her personal circumstances.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Ruth 4:14 when the women bless Naomi for not being left without a kinsman?
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness in provision
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:14 highlights God's faithfulness in providing a kinsman-redeemer, demonstrating His covenantal care and provision for His people.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by the genealogy listed in Ruth 4:18-22?
options: God's sovereign orchestration of history leading to David
The rejection of Gentiles from God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign orchestration of history leading to David
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:18-22 traces the lineage to David, showing God's sovereign hand in history to bring forth the king, which is central to Messianic hope (cf. Acts 13:22).

questions.question: How does Boaz’s declaration in Ruth 4:10 foreshadow Christ’s redemptive role?
options: Boaz redeems Ruth to raise up the dead's name, prefiguring Christ as Redeemer
Boaz prophesies the coming Messiah explicitly
questions.correctAnswer: Boaz redeems Ruth to raise up the dead's name, prefiguring Christ as Redeemer
questions.explanation: In Ruth 4:10, Boaz's redeeming act anticipates Christ’s role as the ultimate Redeemer who restores life and inheritance to the spiritually dead.

questions.question: What broader redemptive theme is highlighted by the communal witness of elders and people in Ruth 4:9-11?
options: The importance of covenant community in legitimizing redemption
The supremacy of individual faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of covenant community in legitimizing redemption
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:9-11 shows elders and people as witnesses, affirming the communal nature of covenant and redemption, echoing broader biblical themes of corporate witness (Deut 19:15).

questions.question: How does the marriage of Boaz and Ruth in Ruth 4:13 reflect God's plan for sanctification and covenant continuity?
options: Their union preserves the family line and exemplifies God’s sanctifying covenant care
It creates a new religious sect
questions.correctAnswer: Their union preserves the family line and exemplifies God’s sanctifying covenant care
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:13 shows the marriage as God's means to continue the family line and covenant promises, illustrating sanctification through covenantal faithfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the story in Ruth 4 is merely a human legal transaction without divine significance. What does Ruth 4:4-5 actually teach about God's redemptive plan?
options: It teaches divine providence and foreshadows Christ’s redeeming work
It is purely secular and has no theological meaning
It denies God’s involvement in history
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches divine providence and foreshadows Christ’s redeeming work
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:4-5 presents Boaz’s legal redemption as a divine act of covenant faithfulness, prefiguring Christ’s redemptive work, contradicting sceptical views of it as mere human transaction.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight arises from combining Ruth 4:6 and Ruth 4:8 regarding human limitations and God's provision?
options: Human inability opens way for God’s provision through another redeemer
Redemption is purely a human act
God does not intervene in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Human inability opens way for God’s provision through another redeemer
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:6 shows the first kinsman’s inability to redeem due to self-interest, and 4:8 shows Boaz stepping in, illustrating how human failure allows God to provide a faithful redeemer.

questions.question: What does the naming of Obed in Ruth 4:17 symbolize in the biblical narrative?
options: God’s faithfulness to preserve the Messianic line
The establishment of a new religion
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to preserve the Messianic line
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:17’s naming of Obed, ancestor of David, symbolizes God’s covenant faithfulness to preserve the Messianic line despite hardship and foreign lineage.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most evident in Ruth 4:1-2 through Boaz’s actions at the city gate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice and righteousness
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:1-2 shows Boaz initiating legal proceedings with elders, demonstrating God’s attribute of justice and righteousness in upholding covenantal laws.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Ruth 4:11 and Ruth 4:12 convey about God’s blessing on covenant families?
options: God blesses covenant families with fruitfulness and lasting legacy
God punishes covenant families with exile
God demands isolation from the community
God replaces covenant families with new ones
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses covenant families with fruitfulness and lasting legacy
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:11-12 bless Naomi’s family, comparing them to Rachel, Leah, and Pharez, highlighting God’s blessing of fruitfulness and legacy within covenant families.

questions.question: How does the role of Naomi in Ruth 4:16 emphasize the theme of covenant community and nurture?
options: Naomi nurses and cares for Obed, showing covenant family nurture
questions.correctAnswer: Naomi nurses and cares for Obed, showing covenant family nurture
questions.explanation: Ruth 4:16 describes Naomi taking Obed into her bosom and nursing him, emphasizing the vital role of covenant community in nurturing God’s promises.
